citation: Medstrand, van de Lagemaat & Mager 2002, Genome Res
authors: Medstrand P, van de Lagemaat LN, Mager DL.
finding: L1 and all LTR classes, particularly those in the same orientation as the nearest gene, are significantly underrepresented within genes.

authors: Han JS, Szak ST, Boeke JD.
finding: Sense L1 ORF sequence impairs transcriptional elongation (A-rich bias, length-dependent); antisense L1 causes premature polyadenylation.
relevance_to_our_result: L1-specific. Cannot explain the Alu-dominated signal.

citation: Roy-Engel et al. 2005, Cytogenet Genome Res
authors: Roy-Engel AM, El-Sawy M, Farooq L, Odom GL, Perepelitsa-Belancio V, Bruch H, Oyeniran OO, Deininger PL.
finding: Alu and L1 carry canonical AATAAA polyadenylation signals, commonly created in the A-rich tails of BOTH SINEs and LINEs. Computational analysis of 34 genes found an orientation bias: fewer L1s and Alus carrying a pA signal in the SAME orientation as the gene. Individually the Alu pA signal is weak.
relevance_to_our_result: Mechanism candidate for Alu, and the source of the A-rich-tail idea. n=34 genes is small.

authors: Gal-Mark N, Schwartz S, Ast G.
finding: Intronic Alu can acquire mutations generating functional splice sites (exonization). Most exonizations occur in the right arm of ANTISENSE Alu and are alternatively spliced.
relevance_to_our_result: Runs the OTHER way: antisense Alu is the exonization-prone orientation, so this predicts selection against ANTISENSE, opposite to what we observe. Tension worth naming.

authors: Andrew B Conley; I King Jordan.
finding: TE sequences within human introns show an ANTISENSE orientation bias, proposed to reflect selection against sense TEs because they terminate host transcription. Characterised >9,000 TE-derived transcription termination sites serving 5,747 human genes across 8 cell types.
relevance_to_our_result: This provides a plausible mechanism context for the Alu orientation pattern; it does not directly explain our callset.

authors: Mansoureh Tajaddod; Andrea Tanzer; Konstantin Licht; Michael T Wolfinger; Stefan Badelt; Florian Huber; Oliver Pusch; Sandy Schopoff; Michael Janisiw; Ivo Hofacker; Michael F Jantsch.
finding: Genome-wide analysis of Alu insertion patterns in transcribed regions. INVERTED Alu pairs repress gene expression; the effect is independent of known dsRNA sensors and instead impairs transcriptional elongation.
relevance_to_our_result: A second, orientation-dependent Alu mechanism — but about inverted PAIRS, not single insertions.
